excerpt: Omnea is a London-founded AI procurement platform that runs intake, approvals, supplier risk and source-to-pay workflows with AI agents. Raised a $20M Series A led by Accel.
content:
Omnea is procurement software. It sits between employees who want to buy something and the finance, legal, security and procurement teams that must approve it, and automates the full supplier lifecycle from intake to renewal. The company now calls its product the Agentic Operating System for Procurement: AI agents handle steps such as intake, document review, approvals, supplier performance and risk mitigation, while human procurement and finance officers stay in control. Omnea says it connects to existing systems rather than replacing them; its Series A announcement described it working alongside tools such as Coupa, SAP Ariba and NetSuite, and launching expanded AI features and third-party risk management products.

Omnea was founded in 2022 by Ben Freeman, its CEO, and Ben Allen. The founding team came from the cybersecurity company Tessian, which Proofpoint acquired in 2023. Omnea's announcement said it takes an average of six months and more than 11 stakeholders for a new tool to go from identification to purchase, the problem it set out to fix.

Funding

On 14 October 2024 Omnea announced a $20 million Series A led by Accel, with First Round Capital and Point Nine, which had led a previously unannounced $5 million seed round. Angels included former Workday CTO David Clarke, former Stripe COO Claire Hughes Johnson and Asana COO Anne Raimondi. The company said its revenue had grown eightfold in the previous year and that it planned to triple headcount and open in the US; Tech.eu named customers including AlphaSights, McAfee, Onfido and TeamViewer.

Pricing

Omnea does not publish prices. Its website asks companies to book a demo.

Who it suits

Omnea suits procurement, finance and IT leaders at mid-sized and large companies where buying software and services involves many reviewers and suppliers. Small businesses with a handful of suppliers are unlikely to need it.

We have not tested Omnea. This page is based on Omnea's website and Series A press release and on Tech.eu.
